Feluda.description: A private investigator and the protagonist of the stories, also known as Pradosh C. Mitter or Mr Mitter.

Jatayu.description: A popular thriller writer and close friend of Feluda who uses the pen name Jatayu.

Tapesh.description: Feluda's cousin and the narrator of the stories, often referred to by his nickname Topshe.

Srinath.description: A domestic helper who is asked to make tea for the group.

Mahitosh Roy.description: A theatre actor who approaches Feluda for help after receiving anonymous threats and later disappears.

Jaganmoy Bhattacharya.description: A former actor at Apsara Theatre who was replaced by Mahitosh Roy and is mentioned as a possible suspect.

Nepal Lahiri.description: Nepal Lahiri is the lead actor at Apsara Theatre, whose murder is central to the plot.

Sherlock Holmes.description: A famous fictional detective created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, referenced as an inspiration.

Watson.description: Dr. John Watson, Sherlock Holmes's friend and chronicler, referenced in comparison to Feluda and Topshe.

Conan Doyle.description: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, the creator of Sherlock Holmes.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, referenced as the setting for Lalmohan Babu's popularity.

Apsara Theatre.description: Apsara Theatre is a prominent theatre company where Nepal Lahiri was a star actor and Mahitosh Roy currently works.

Prafulla.description: A play being performed at Apsara Theatre, with Mahitosh Roy in a small role.

Rupmanch.description: A previous theatre company where Mahitosh Roy worked before joining Apsara.

Ballygunj.description: A locality in Kolkata, India, where Mahitosh Roy lives.

Five Panditia Place.description: The specific address in Ballygunj where Mahitosh Roy resides.

daalmut.description: A popular Indian snack made from fried lentils and spices.

Dinabandhu.description: The loyal bearer of Mahitosh Roy, who has served him for twenty-two years and assists Feluda in the investigation.

Subodh Adhikari.description: The Officer-in-Charge (OC) and police inspector at Bhawanipore police station handling the case of Mahitosh Roy's disappearance.

Bhawanipore.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta, location of the police station involved in the investigation.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in India where the story is set.

Shyambazar.description: A well-known area in Calcutta, location of the Apsara Theatre.

bearer.description: A domestic servant, often responsible for personal service in Indian households.

supari.description: Areca nut, commonly chewed in India, often as a mouth freshener.

Kailash Banerjee.description: The manager of Apsara Theatre, who provides information about Mahitosh Roy and other actors.

Nirmal Bose Street.description: A street address in the city where Jaganmoy Bhattacharya currently resides.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or gatekeeper, commonly employed at buildings or compounds in India.

divan.description: A long, low sofa without a back or arms, often used for sitting or reclining in South Asian homes.

Sudhendu Chakravarty.description: The new actor employed by Apsara Theatre to replace Mahitosh Roy.

Shivtosh.description: Mahitosh Roy's younger brother, estranged from him due to family disputes over inheritance.

Anup Sengupta.description: A friend of Shivtosh Roy whose house provided Shivtosh with an alibi.

Sasadhar Chatterjee.description: An actor who works for Rupam Theatre and was the friend Nepal Lahiri was visiting when he was killed.

Sardar Shankar Road.description: A street in Calcutta where Anup Sengupta's house is located.

Digha.description: A seaside town in West Bengal, India, where Feluda and his friends travel for a break.

Rupam Theatre.description: A rival theatre company where Sasadhar Chatterjee works.

Nakuleshwar Bhattacharya Lane.description: The address where Nepal Lahiri lived.

Alamgeer.description: A new play planned by Apsara Theatre, with Nepal Lahiri originally set to play the main role.

Moti Mistri Lane.description: The alley where Nepal Lahiri was killed.

namaskar.description: 'Namaskar' is a respectful Indian greeting or farewell, similar to 'hello' or 'goodbye.'

Inspector Bhowmik.description: The police inspector in charge of the murder case.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, commonly chewed in India.

Dharani Sanyal.description: The seniormost artiste at Apsara, with twenty-six years of experience.

Dipen Bose.description: An actor at Apsara who joined the theatre with Nepal Lahiri.

Bhujanga Ray.description: An actor at Apsara and close friend of Nepal Lahiri.

Kalikinkar Ghoshal.description: A friend of Dharani Sanyal, whose house hosted a keertan session.

Omega.description: A luxury Swiss watch brand; Nepal Lahiri's expensive watch that went missing.

Amherst Row.description: A residential area where Sudhendu Chakravarty lives.

keertan.description: A devotional singing session, often involving group chanting of religious songs.

snuff.description: A powdered tobacco product inhaled through the nose, commonly used in India.
